intent: issues.md → GitHub Issues; new file-github-issue procedure
notes: **Retired `.gator/issues.md` as the primary issue tracker.** Per the 2026-08-04 design outline at `.gator/vault/artifacts/2026-08-04-github-issue-tracking-outline.md` and the Architect's decision to migrate. The public monorepo has outgrown a flat repo-local markdown file — for a public Apache 2.0 project with release cadence, packaging boundaries, and (soon) external contributors, GitHub Issues is the right system of record.

**New tracker**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/cumberland-laboratories/gator/issues) on `cumberland-laboratories/gator`, organized by the [Gator project board](https://github.com/users/cumberland-laboratories/projects/1). Metadata contract: `Priority` (P0/P1/P2/P3), `Area` (Core CLI / Dashboard / Hooks / Charters / Loop / Enterprise / Packaging / Release / Docs), `Status` (Todo / In Progress / Done). Labels layered on top for cross-cutting tags (`bug`, `hooks`, `dashboard`, `packaging`, `maintenance`, etc.).
**Four issues migrated** from the old `.gator/issues.md` (all originally Open):

**Two originally-resolved items** (#2 Dashboard false alarm; #6 migrate_layout Step 5 dir conflicts — shipped in v2.5.4 commit `5453f8b`) were NOT migrated: they're already Done, their resolution notes are preserved in git history via `git log --follow -- .gator/issues.md`, and re-filing them just to close them would be paperwork without signal. The retirement stub references both explicitly so the trail is walkable.
